default_mode.description: Default mode: 'encrypt', 'decrypt', 'cat', 'keychange', or 'unixcrypt'. Overrides default mode behavior. Case-insensitive. Empty string means rely on command name (ccencrypt/ccdecrypt/ccat) or -e/-d/-c.

default_suffix.description: Suffix to append/remove instead of '.cpt'. Must start with a dot (e.g., '.cpt'). Empty string uses .cpt.

use_brave.description: If true, disable double-key prompt (--brave). Not recommended unless you know what you're doing.

use_timid.description: If true, enforce double-key prompt (--timid). This is the default; --brave overrides.

strict_suffix.description: If true, refuse to encrypt files that already have the suffix (--strictsuffix). No effect in decrypt/keychange mode.

use_tmpfiles.description: If true, use temporary files instead of in-place overwrite (--tmpfiles). Less secure (original data remains on disk), but safer against system crashes.

use_symlinks.description: If true, process symbolic links (--symlinks). By default, symlinks are ignored except in cat/unixcrypt modes.

envvar.description: Environment variable from which to read the encryption/decryption key. Unsafe on systems where environment variables are visible via `ps`. Implies --brave unless --timid follows. See -E option.

keyfile.description: File path from which to read the key as the first line. Use '-' for stdin. In keychange mode, reads two lines. See -k option.

prompt.description: Custom prompt string instead of 'Enter encryption/decryption key: '. Useful in scripts. See -P option.

follow_symlinks.description: If true, follow symlinks to subdirectories during recursive traversal (--rec-symlinks).

keyref.description: Path to a previously encrypted file (with the same key) used to verify the key before processing (--keyref). Implies --brave unless --timid follows.

force.description: If true, overwrite existing or write-protected files without prompting (--force). Use with caution.
